paragraphs: Long ago, in a peaceful kingdom, there lived a King who had twelve daughters.
They were kind, graceful, and beautiful.
Every night, the twelve princesses went to sleep together in one great chamber, and every night the doors were locked tight.
Yet each morning, when the servants came to wake them…
Something strange was always found.
Their shoes were worn thin.
As if they had danced through the night.
The King was puzzled.
Where could his daughters be going? How could they leave without anyone seeing them?
At last, he made an announcement throughout the land.
“Whoever discovers where my daughters dance at night shall choose one of them for his wife… and one day be king.”
But there was also a warning.
Anyone who tried and failed would lose his life.
Many brave men came.
Kings’ sons. Noble lords. Adventurers seeking glory.
They watched. They listened.
But each night they fell into deep sleep.
And each morning, the shoes were worn through again.
And each brave man was gone.
One day, an old soldier, tired from long years of travel, passed through the forest near the kingdom.
There he met a quiet old woman who asked where he was going.
“I do not know,” he said softly. “But I would like to find the secret of the dancing princesses.”
The old woman smiled.
“That is not so hard,” she said. “Only do not drink the wine they offer you… and pretend to sleep.”
Then she gave him a magical cloak.
“When you wear this,” she said, “you will become invisible.”
The soldier thanked her and went to the King.
That evening, he was placed in the chamber near the princesses.
Soon, the eldest princess brought him a cup of wine.
He poured it away quietly.
Then he lay down and pretended to sleep.
When the clock struck midnight, the princesses rose.
They laughed softly as they dressed in shining gowns.
The youngest sister whispered, “I feel uneasy tonight.”
But the eldest said, “Do not be afraid. Everyone else has failed before.”
Then something wonderful happened.
The eldest princess clapped her hands.
And her bed sank into the floor.
A hidden staircase appeared.
One by one, the princesses stepped down into the secret below.
And quietly… the invisible soldier followed.
At the bottom of the stairs lay a path through three enchanted forests.
The first forest shimmered with silver leaves. The second glowed with gold. The third sparkled like diamonds.
The soldier gently broke a small branch from each tree to keep as proof.
Each time, the youngest princess grew more afraid.
“I heard a sound,” she whispered.
But the eldest always said, “It is only our princes welcoming us.”
Beyond the forests lay a great lake.
Twelve little boats waited.
And in each boat sat a handsome prince.
The princesses stepped in.
And the soldier stepped invisibly into the boat of the youngest sister.
As they rowed, the prince beside her said, “Our boat feels heavier tonight.”
The princess smiled. “It must be the warm air.”
And on they went.
On the far shore stood a glowing castle filled with music.
Horns sang. Trumpets called. Soft laughter drifted through the air.
Inside, the princes and princesses danced.
And though unseen…
The soldier danced too.
Whenever the princesses set down their cups of wine, the invisible soldier drank them.
And when they lifted the cups again…
They were empty.
The youngest sister trembled.
“Something is wrong,” she whispered.
But the eldest laughed gently.
“You worry too much.”
They danced until the stars faded.
Until their shoes were worn thin once more.
And then they returned the way they had come.
The soldier hurried ahead.
He slipped back into his chamber.
And soon the princesses followed, tired but smiling.
They believed their secret was safe.
For three nights, the soldier watched.
For three nights, he followed.
On the third night, he carried away a small golden cup as proof.
At last, he was called before the King.
The princesses listened from behind a door.
The soldier placed the silver, gold, and diamond branches before the throne.
He set down the golden cup.
And he told the story.
The King turned to his daughters.
They saw there was no hiding anymore.
And they nodded.
“It is true,” they said.
The King sighed, but he was no longer angry.
Only glad the truth was known.
Then he turned to the soldier.
“Which of my daughters will you choose?”
The soldier smiled gently.
“I am not young,” he said. “I will choose the eldest.”
And so the eldest princess became his bride.
The secret door was closed forever.
The enchanted dances ended.
And the twelve sisters slept peacefully each night…
With shoes that stayed whole by morning.
